_comment: The malfunction procedures for the failure catalog's caution lights (data/failures.json, slice 9a), in every mission's CSM checklist book after its flight's lists (ChecklistBook.load_default()). A failure opens its procedure as it comes. The launch vehicle's lights (slice 9d) get the launch aborts' procedure, from the CSM Apollo Operations Handbook's section 2.9 [adapted]. The simulator's own [adapted]: each light's meaning is the C&W table's (CSM Apollo Operations Handbook, SM2A-03-BLOCK II-(1), pp. 2.10-5 to 2.10-8) [published]; the actions are those the simulated systems have.

steps.text: CRYO PRESS: an O2 or H2 tank's pressure out of limits (the HUD's CRYO line)
MASTER ALARM - press
An O2 tank at zero: the fuel cells on its valve module fail next. CM POWER - EMER, the emergency power-down
Each fuel cell whose FC light comes on - off its buses (FC 1, FC 2, FC 3)
FC 1, 2 or 3: a fuel cell's flow, temperature or pH out of limits
MASTER ALARM - press
The failed cell - off its buses (its FC switch, MDC-3): the other two carry the load
MN BUS A and B above 26.25 V (no UNDERVOLT light); if not, CM POWER - EMER

checklists.title: Malfunction: SM RCS A, B, C or D

steps.text: SM RCS A, B, C or D: a quad's secondary fuel pressure out of limits
MASTER ALARM - press
The quad's RCS QUAD switch - off (MDC-2): isolate it
Its axes on the quad opposite: pitch on A and C, yaw on B and D. The autopilot turns slower about them
CMC: the computer has failed. Its DSKY is dark and its autopilot stopped
MASTER ALARM - press
ATT SOURCE - SCS: the SCS holds the attitude
Houston's PADs from here: each burn on the SCS, turned to the PAD's R, P and Y on the FDAI's GDC angles, to the EMS's count of its DVC (EMS FUNCTION DV, THRUST ON)
ISS: the IMU has failed. NO ATT on the DSKY: the CMC has no attitude
MASTER ALARM - press
ATT SOURCE - SCS: the SCS holds the attitude
No coarse align, P51 or P52 brings the platform back: the burns on the SCS, to the EMS's count

checklists.title: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID

steps.text: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID: a launch vehicle engine out, the vehicle's rates past the EDS's limits, or the IU's guidance lost
With the tower on and EDS AUTO: two S-IC engines out, or the rates, abort on their own, and the tower pulls the CM away (mode I)
ABORT light or Houston's 'Abort': the translation controller's handle - counterclockwise
Mode I: the canards at 11 s, then the tower's jettison and the chutes as the ELS brings them
Modes II to IV: the CSM leaves the launch vehicle 3 s after the handle; the handle back at neutral ends the SM's +X jets
Mode II: CM/SM SEP, lift up; ELS LOGIC and ELS AUTO on
Mode III: Houston's PAD, the SPS's retrograde burn (P40); CM/SM SEP; half lift, rolled 60 degrees to the south; ELS LOGIC and ELS AUTO on
Mode IV: Houston's PAD, the SPS's burn into orbit (P40)
